Review 1 of 1.24.33: PowerPoint files in Slides (PPTX_TEXT, PPTX_READ, PPTX_WRITE, SLIDES_PPTX)
=========================================================================================

Run: node tests/fixtures/pptx_review1_1233/replay.js [src]      (about 10 seconds; python3 with lxml and
python-pptx, the ISO/IEC 29500 schemas and LibreOffice are used when present, else those cases say SKIP)
Against src/lantern.inner.html 1.24.33 as of 2026-11-21 (sha256 085761f4fe8a...):
    301 cases: 263 AGREE, 38 DISAGREE

What was made: 41 files in decks/ (make_decks.py, gen_other.py, pp.py make them): decks from python-pptx with
PowerPoint's own template (every usual layout, numbered lists in five schemes, bullets turned on and off by the
shape, the layout and the master, tables with joined cells, six kinds of chart, pictures in seven formats,
groups, text boxes out of order, the characters people type, notes), the same decks as LibreOffice saves them,
a Strict file, packages written by hand as Google Slides and Keynote export them, one as PowerPoint 365 writes
(slide order unlike the file names, absolute targets, sections, a hidden slide, mc:AlternateContent, comments),
damaged files, and files that are not presentations. 49 decks written as Slides and Chat make them
(cases_write.js) saved and checked with the schemas, python-pptx and LibreOffice in one batch.
renders/ holds three LibreOffice drawings of Lantern's saves (named below).

What was not run: PowerPoint, Google Slides and Keynote themselves (none on this machine). Where a finding says
what PowerPoint does, it says how sure it is; LibreOffice and python-pptx were run.

What held up well (all AGREE): every saved file is valid in every part, python-pptx finds every title and
LibreOffice makes a page a slide, for all 49 saves and for every deck read and saved again; bullets inherited
through shape, layout, master and txStyles (including buNone in the layout over the master's bullet, and a layout
giving a bullet back over a master without one); subtitles; tables with joined cells; charts as tables; Google's
and Keynote's exports (data-descriptor zips, explicit bullets, empty runs, placeholders placed only by the
layout); LibreOffice's saves; Strict; sldIdLst order; hidden slides, comments, video, Visio and Excel objects,
SmartArt said with their slides; sixty and eighty slides; emoji, CJK, Arabic, entities, links; Open .pptx and
Save .pptx and Chat's Save .pptx.


THE DISAGREEMENTS, WORST FIRST
------------------------------

1. [high] Side-by-side boxes whose tops are not exactly level are read in the wrong order.
   Cases: d07-steps-uneven, d07-columns, d05-text-beside-chart (medium).
   Input: three step boxes along a line, "1. Isolate" (top 2.3 in), "2. Lock" (2.0 in), "3. Test" (2.15 in);
   Before/After columns whose tops differ by 0.02 in; points on the left and a chart 0.15 in higher on the right.
   Lantern: "2. Lock, 1. Isolate, 3. Test"; "After ... Before ..."; the chart's numbers before the points.
   Right: left to right along a line: 1, 2, 3; Before, then After; the points, then the chart.
   Why it matters: hand-placed boxes are almost never exactly level. A trainer's three steps come into
   Lantern numbered in one order and read in another; a before/after slide reads backwards. Nothing is said.
   Traced: PPTX_READ sorts by Math.round(y / (H/24)): a band boundary can fall between two boxes a hair apart
   (0.31 in bands on a 7.5 in slide), and then y wins over x. Boxes that overlap vertically by most of their
   height are on one line whatever their tops.

2. [high] Comparison slides: each heading is read away from its own points.
   Case: d01-comparison (also seen in LibreOffice's and the Strict copy of the deck).
   Input: PowerPoint's Comparison layout: "Electric" over "Quiet / Charge overnight", "Gas (LPG)" over
   "Change the cylinder outdoors / No charging time".
   Lantern: Electric, Gas (LPG), then all four points: the reader cannot tell which points are gas.
   Right: Electric and its two points, then Gas (LPG) and its two (the slide's own order in the file, and how a
   person reads two columns).
   Why it matters: the layout exists to compare two things; read across, it compares nothing. It is one of
   PowerPoint's nine standard layouts.

3. [high] Saved slides with more text than fits run off the slide in PowerPoint, and nothing is said.
   Cases: w-fifteen-fits, w-pic-text-fits (high), w-twelve-fits (medium).
   Input: 15 bullets; seven sentence-long points beside a photo (the text box is 56% wide); 12 one-word points.
   Lantern: writes them at 24 pt with <a:normAutofit/> and no fontScale; the save's notes are empty.
   Right: store the size that fits (normAutofit fontScale and lnSpcReduction, which PowerPoint draws as stored),
   or say "more than fits (slide n)". PowerPoint does not shrink on opening: it applies normAutofit's stored
   scale (100% when none is stored) and refits only when the text is edited (as python-pptx documents for its own
   files; sure for PowerPoint 2016/365 desktop as far as I know, not checked here). LibreOffice shrinks on its own,
   so its PDF looks fine and hides this.
   Why it matters: Lantern's own Present mode shrinks text to fit, so the trainer never sees a problem; the
   colleague opening the .pptx in PowerPoint sees the last points hanging below the slide, cut off in the show.
   Traced: the writer's "long" note is raised only when tables push past the box (tTop); a slide of text alone
   never moves tTop.

4. [medium] A slide with an empty title box comes back with its text as its title (and the note is wrong).
   Cases: w-no-title-roundtrip (Lantern's own save read back), d15-empty-title-box shows the same on a deck.
   Input: a Slides slide with no title and one line of text, saved as .pptx and opened again.
   Lantern: h = "A line with no title above it", body empty, and it says "a slide with no title box takes its
   short first line as its title" - but the slide has a title box, empty.
   Right: no title, the line as text. PowerPoint shows that slide with an empty title ("Click to add title").
   Why it matters: a round trip through PowerPoint's format changes the deck: the line becomes a big orange
   title, and saving again moves it into the title box for good.
   Traced: the title-from-first-line rule runs whenever no title placeholder had text; it should run only when
   the slide has no title placeholder at all.

5. [medium] One damaged part refuses the whole deck.
   Cases: d18-bad-slide, d18-bad-notes, d18-bad-core (medium), d18-bad-layout (low).
   Input: one slide's XML cut short; slide 1's notes page damaged; docProps/core.xml (the title and author)
   damaged; one layout damaged.
   Lantern: "the file is damaged: a part of it is not readable XML" - no slides at all.
   Right: the other slides (and every slide, for a damaged notes page, layout or properties part), with what was
   lost said: "1 slide that could not be read, left out (slide 2)", "the notes of slide 1". The reader already has
   that note for a missing slide; a slide that will not parse should take the same path. (PowerPoint offers to
   repair such a file and keeps what it can.)
   Why it matters: a deck that came off a failing USB stick or a cut email attachment is all the trainer has;
   losing the talk over its author field is the worst outcome.

6. [medium] Dark decks are saved with Dark 1 white, so tables and shapes added later in PowerPoint are unreadable.
   Case: w-theme-dark-scheme. Render: renders/night_deck_table_inserted_later.png.
   Input: any deck in Night (Slides' default), Chalkboard, Ocean or Sunset, saved; then a table and a shape
   inserted (here with python-pptx, drawn by LibreOffice) as a colleague would in PowerPoint.
   Lantern: theme1.xml has dk1 = the deck's text colour (white) and lt1 = its background (near black).
   What shows: PowerPoint's default style for a new table (Medium Style 2 - Accent 1, the def Lantern's
   tableStyles.xml names) draws body cells as dk1 text on a 20% tint of Accent 1: white on pale peach. A new
   shape gets lt1 (near black) text on orange.
   Right: keep Dark 1 dark and Light 1 light, and map the slide to them as PowerPoint's dark themes do
   (clrMap bg1="dk1" tx1="lt1" bg2="dk2" tx2="lt2"). The slides as saved look the same; what is added afterwards
   is readable.
   Why it matters: every deck Slides saves by default is dark; the first table a colleague adds is unreadable,
   and they will blame the file.

7. [medium] A photo turned in PowerPoint comes in sideways, without a word.
   Case: d06-turned (and d06-cropped, low: a crop is lost the same way).
   Input: a landscape photo turned a quarter (xfrm rot=5400000), shown portrait in PowerPoint.
   Lantern: keeps the file's pixels (landscape) and says nothing.
   Right: turn it as PowerPoint shows it (Lantern already redraws every picture on a canvas in
   slidesPptx.shrink; rot, flipH/flipV and srcRect can be applied there), or say "the picture on slide 12 was
   turned in PowerPoint; turn it here". Phone photos rotated in PowerPoint are common in site decks.

8. [medium] A long title runs off the top of the slide.
   Case: w-long-title-fits. Render: renders/long_title-1.png (LibreOffice: the first line is gone).
   Input: a 150-character title. Lantern writes it at 40 pt in a box anchored at its foot; four lines grow upward
   past the slide's top edge.
   Right: store it shrunk to fit, or say the title is too long for slide n.

9. [medium] A .pptx with a password is called "an older Office file (.doc, .xls or .ppt)".
   Case: w-locked. Input: an encrypted .pptx (a compound file holding EncryptionInfo and EncryptedPackage, as
   PowerPoint writes it with File > Info > Protect > Encrypt with Password).
   Right: "this PowerPoint file is locked with a password: open it in PowerPoint, remove the password, save,
   and open it again". The current message sends the trainer looking for an old file they do not have.

10. [medium] Lettered and roman-numbered lists come in as 1. 2. 3.
    Cases: d02-letters (a) b)), d02-roman (I. II. III.).
    Right: keep the scheme (<ol type="a">, <ol type="I">, and buAutoNum alphaLcParenR / romanUcPeriod on save),
    or say it was changed. A quiz slide whose answer is "b)" no longer has a b).

11. [medium] A table cell that spans past the last row is saved as a broken table.
    Case: w-rowspan-over-consistent. Render: renders/rowspan_past_end-1.png.
    Input: <td rowspan="3"> in a table of two rows (what is left when a row is deleted in an editor; browsers
    draw it as two). Lantern writes rowSpan="3" with only two rows. LibreOffice draws an empty filled cell and
    does not join the cells. PowerPoint is strict about table merges; I expect a repair prompt but did not see it.
    Right: clamp the span to the rows there are (rowSpan="2").

LOW
12. Chart numbers lose their format: a pie of 50%/30%/20% reads 0.5/0.3/0.2 (d05-pie-percent); months read
    45658.0 (d05-dates: date categories are day numbers with a date format code). Apply the cache's formatCode
    at least for % and dates.
13. Speaker notes: a blank line (the trainer's pause) is dropped (d09-blank-line, and w-notes-blank-back for
    Lantern's own saves: the writer keeps the blank paragraph, the reader drops it); a line break inside a
    paragraph (Shift+Enter) becomes a space (d09-line-break).
14. Sections (a long course's Part 1 / Part 2 in PowerPoint's slide list) are not kept and not said
    (d10-sections).
15. Saving: a table's <caption> vanishes without a word (w-caption-kept); a <pre> code block's lines are run
    into one line (w-pre-lines: an Arduino sketch on a slide becomes unreadable); a second paragraph inside a
    numbered item is written at the margin, left of its number (w-li-p-indent); a table inside a list item is
    moved after the list (w-table-in-li-order).
16. A link whose address holds a space is written as Target="https://example.org/my manual.pdf" (w-link-space);
    percent-encode it as a browser does. Not sure PowerPoint objects.
17. Right-to-left paragraphs (rtl="1", right-aligned) lose their direction (d08-rtl-direction); All Caps (cap=
    "all") text reads in its stored case, "Warning" where PowerPoint shows WARNING (d08-caps).
18. Plainer refusals: an Impress .odp and a Keynote .key are "a zip file with no PowerPoint presentation in
    it" (w-odp, w-key: say what they are and to export as .pptx); a PDF renamed .pptx is "not a zip file"
    (w-pdf). A .ppsx/.potx/.pptm keeps its extension in the deck's name ("w_show.ppsx", w-ppsx-name). Open
    .pptx's file chooser accepts only .pptx, though .ppsx (a PowerPoint Show, how decks are often handed
    out) and .potx open fine (g-open-accept).
